name: One session counts once: device-day median collapse
non_visual_rationale: A collapse is the absence of a difference between two stored files; nothing renders. No template, string, style or route is touched, and at launch the observation log is empty, so the published surface is byte-identical either way. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
criteria_delivered: 1. Per (spot, day, device) the fit collapses samples to the median SAMPLE before anything else weighs them. The collapse runs inside correction-file.ts's estimateOf, which is the one door every key's evidence passes through, so n, the distinct-reporter count and the n inside se's physical floor are all already post-collapse counts rather than three places each remembering to subtract.

2. A device repeating its report five times in one session leaves every stored byte identical. Proven as literal string equality between two whole correction files, not as a corridor on b: before this step the five repeats stored n = 26 where the same mornings reported once stored n = 22.
3. The surviving sample is the session's MEDIAN, proven against a second, simpler median written in the test, and it is a sample somebody actually reported rather than a manufactured average.
criteria_deferred: Criterion 3 of the roadmap step ('collapse happens before winsorization and concordance, in the 06 section 6.2 order') CANNOT BE TESTED HERE and is not silently dropped. There is no second stage yet for the collapse to be before. The order becomes observable at 04-02, where winsorizing an uncollapsed list would let a repeated wild claim survive its own fence by dominating the day median; 04-02 owns the test that proves it. Recorded here so the criterion is carried, not lost.
scope_note: THE ROADMAP'S 'FIRST MOVE' INSTRUCTION IS STALE AND WAS NOT FOLLOWED. All six slice-04 steps carry the identical line 'delete its entry from PENDING_SLICES in tests/acceptance/.../steps/support/pending-slices.ts', naming a cucumber scaffold, a .feature file and a steps/support directory that do not exist for this feature anywhere in the tree. This feature's acceptance tests are vitest files driving the real runLearningFitOnce port (18 of them, 01-05 through 03-04), and 03-04's own red_evidence records its crafter writing the acceptance example first rather than unskipping one. This step follows the shape phases 1 through 3 actually shipped: acceptance test authored here, watched RED, then GREEN. The roadmap named weights.ts and estimate.ts; estimate.ts was NOT touched (see the design decision below) and residuals.ts and correction-file.ts were, because the sample has to carry its day and the collapse has to reach the one place a key's evidence is counted.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: THE WEIGHING ROOM IS A NEW MODULE, NOT PART OF estimate.ts. WHY-NEW-FILE: src/learning/weights.ts. CLOSEST-EXISTING: src/learning/estimate.ts. EXTENSION-COST: estimate.ts is the general weighted-mean and standard-error primitive read by the height lane, the score lane AND the gate's own error floor; it consumes a finished list of weighted values and never looks at who reported them or when. Folding a per-session collapse into it would make every reader of a weighted mean depend on sample identity fields (day, device) the primitive deliberately cannot see. PARALLEL-RATIONALE: the accepted roadmap names src/learning/weights.ts as this slice's owned path in all six steps, and 06 section 6 is a different stage from section 6.1's precision weight -- the weighing room CHANGES THE SAMPLE LIST (dropping repeats now, clipping and reweighting in later steps), while estimate.ts consumes a list and never changes it.

A SAMPLE WHOSE DAY CANNOT BE READ IS ITS OWN SESSION, never merged with another. 06 section 6.2 says 'per (spot, day, device)' without saying what happens when the day is missing. src/learning/inputs.ts reads rows permissively by design, so a row with no observed_at reaches the score lane (the height lane needs the hour to pair at all and drops it earlier). Nothing about a row missing its timestamp says it came from the same morning as the one before it, and quietly collapsing two undated samples would throw away evidence on a guess. The stricter reading is also the one that cannot silently shrink n.

THE MEDIAN OF AN EVEN-SIZED SESSION IS THE LOWER OF THE TWO MIDDLES. 06 section 6.2 says 'collapse to the median sample', and a SAMPLE is what the later stages need: 04-02 reads the day-median's own band width off it and every stage reads its own precision weight. An interpolated midpoint between two reports has neither, so an even count has no single middle and a fixed choice has to be made. Lower-middle after a stable sort by value, so the same session always collapses to the same byte.

THE COLLAPSE RUNS ON BOTH RESIDUAL FORMS, height and score. 06 section 6.2 places it under section 6, whose subject is samples in general. It is also forced by criterion 2: collapsing only the height lane would leave the five repeats inflating score_delta's n and se, and the two stored files would differ.

THE COLLAPSE IS KEYED WITHIN A KEY, so (spot, source, lead_bucket, day, device). Two samples one device produced on one day at two different sources are two different models' errors measured on one morning; collapsing across them would average two models into one number. Within one key, two samples from one device on one day ARE the near-duplicate 09 section 13.4 gate 4 names, whether they came from two submissions of one session or from two consecutive hours of one swell, and both collapse -- which is what that gate asks for.
acceptance: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/one-session-counts-once.test.ts, two examples over the real runLearningFitOnce port with an in-memory store. THE ORACLE IS BYTE IDENTITY between two whole correction files, not a corridor on b. Twenty-two mornings at one spot, seven reporters, an alternating spread so se sits above the physical noise floor; the only difference between the two runs is that on the first morning the same device pressed send five times, at 18:41, 18:43, 18:45, 18:47 and 18:49, all inside the same UTC hour so all five pair with that hour's one prediction row. Byte identity is a fair oracle here only because computed_at comes from the run's own injected clock and the record's key order is insertion order over the same fixture; both runs use the same fixed clock and the same spot, source and lead bucket, so nothing but the collapse can move a byte. A corridor on b would have been useless: five IDENTICAL repeats do not move a weighted mean at all, and an implementation that collapsed the value but not the count would pass it while storing a fabricated n and a fabricated se. The second example is the over-fire guard: the honest one-report-per-morning run must still store all 22 mornings and all 7 reporters.
unit_law: Three fast-check properties in tests/unit/learning-weight-laws.test.ts against collapseSessionsToMedian, whose exported signature is its port. (1) MODELLING (Hebert ch.3): any multiset of 1 to 9 samples sharing one day and one device leaves exactly one sample, and its value equals a median computed by a second, simpler implementation living in the test -- the property that separates a median from a mean, a first or a loudest, none of which the acceptance oracle can see because its repeats are identical. (2) INVARIANT: over a free mixture of three days, three devices and undated samples, the output length equals the number of distinct sessions and every survivor is object-identical to one of the inputs, which is what forbids a manufactured average. (3) IDEMPOTENCE: collapsing an already-collapsed list is the identity, so the fit's order of operations cannot silently matter.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) a session counts once, (2) the surviving sample is the session's median, (3) distinct sessions never merge and nothing is invented. Three behaviours, budget 6. Delivered 5: 2 acceptance examples and 3 unit properties.
red_evidence: The acceptance test was written first and run against the 03-04 body. RED with a semantic AssertionError, not a collection or import error: 'five submissions in one session counted as 26 mornings instead of 22: the session was never collapsed', 26 !== 22. Its companion example (the honest run keeping all 22 mornings and 7 reporters) passed on arrival, correctly: that is today's behaviour and the example exists to keep it. The three unit properties were then run against a deliberate identity stub of collapseSessionsToMedian and failed semantically -- 'one device reporting 2 times in one session left 2 samples in the fit' and '2 samples across 1 sessions collapsed to 2' -- before the real body replaced the stub.
falsifiability_evidence: Three controlled mutations, each planted alone against a byte-snapshot of src/learning, each reverted, and the revert verified with diff -r against that snapshot ('REVERT CLEAN: src/learning matches the pre-mutation snapshot byte for byte'), then the suite re-run green. (M1) the session averaged into a manufactured sample instead of taking its median: caught twice, by 'the surviving sample must be the session's median, not its mean, its first or its loudest' and by 'a collapsed sample must be one somebody actually reported, never a manufactured average'. (M2) the first sample of the session taken instead of the median -- the plausible shortcut, and THE ONE THE ACCEPTANCE TEST CANNOT SEE, because five identical repeats have the same first sample as median: caught by the modelling property alone, which is why that property exists. (M3) the session keyed on the device alone, ignoring the day: caught by three tests at once, the invariant property ('2 samples across 2 sessions collapsed to 1') and both acceptance examples ('five submissions in one session counted as 7 mornings instead of 22', 'the honest baseline run must keep all its mornings'). (M4) the collapse removed entirely is the RED observation above.
